name: Terpinen-4-ol

pubchem.title: Terpinen-4-ol
pubchem.description: 4-terpineol is a terpineol that is 1-menthene carrying a hydroxy substituent at position 4. It has a role as an antioxidant, a volatile oil component, an antibacterial agent, an antiparasitic agent, an antineoplastic agent, an anti-inflammatory agent, an apoptosis inducer and a plant metabolite. It is a terpineol and a tertiary alcohol.

studies.title: Lid Wipes Versus Baby Shampoo in Patients With Seborrehic Blepharitis
interventions: Lid wipes containing terpinen-4-ol and sodium hyaluronate
studies.summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the efficacy of lid wipes containing terpinen-4-ol and sodium hyaluronate (Hy-ter®) for the treatment of seborrheic blepharitis compared to baby shampoo.

studies.title: Demodex Blepharitis Treatment Study
studies.summary: This is a randomized clinical trial to determine the safety and efficacy of terpinen-4-ol (T4O), the most active ingredient of tea tree oil (TTO), in eradicating ocular demodicosis (reducing ocular demodex counts and achieving the clinical improvement with minimal or no irritation).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Terpinen-4-ol is a volatile tertiary alcohol and a major component of several highly aromatic essential oils. It is the primary active ingredient in tea tree oil, giving it a characteristic sharp, medicinal, and earthy scent. People encounter it daily in topical skincare products, natural cleaning supplies, and culinary herbs.
consumer_summary.found_in: This molecule is famously abundant in the tea tree (Melaleuca alternifolia), but it is also found in familiar culinary and medicinal plants like lemon, oregano, rosemary, and bay laurel.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to terpinen-4-ol for its potent ability to disrupt bacterial biofilms and combat microscopic parasites like mites. The strongest evidence for its effects comes from human trials, including a systematic review of randomised trials (Oxford level 1a) evaluating its anti-inflammatory properties. Scientists are particularly excited about its potential as a natural anti-infective agent that could be used in dermatology, eye care, and food preservation.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Clinical researchers are investigating if terpinen-4-ol can soothe chronic eye inflammation caused by Demodex mites and seborrheic conditions.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A completed Phase 4 clinical trial (NCT04441528) has evaluated lid wipes versus baby shampoo in patients with seborrheic blepharitis.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether terpinen-4-ol can effectively dismantle stubborn bacterial biofilms, such as those formed by Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind human trial applying a standardized terpinen-4-ol topical treatment to superficial bacterial infections, measuring bacterial load and biofilm reduction over 14 days.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal and observational work points toward potential antineoplastic properties, exploring whether it can induce apoptosis in abnormal cells.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial evaluating topical application of a terpinen-4-ol formulation on superficial skin lesions, measuring lesion size and apoptotic markers over 12 weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether the inhalation of terpinen-4-ol-rich essential oils might influence cognitive clarity and memory retention.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial in healthy human adults, measuring cognitive performance and memory recall tasks before and after ambient diffusion of isolated terpinen-4-ol.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is a systematic review of randomised trials (Oxford 1a) for its anti-inflammatory effects, with a large body of observational and lab work supporting its antimicrobial properties.
